title: Transient headroom brokerage and pro-rated overage reconciliation
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Scope: implement a transient headroom brokerage layer for Dedicated fleets that allows tenants to 'lease' short-duration extra throughput capacity with transparent, pro-rated billing and automated reconciliation. This is intended to cover short spikes without forcing long-term capacity commits or surprise overage invoices.

Goals: 1) Provide an API and operator controls for granting temporary capacity leases (lease size in RPS / tokens-per-minute equivalent), 2) Bill leases pro-rata to actual lease duration and usage, 3) Refund or credit unused portions when leases are preempted or not consumed, 4) Expose observability and safety gates so SREs and account teams can audit and intervene.

Proposal summary: introduce a 'headroom broker' component in the Dedicated control plane. Tenants request a lease via a new endpoint or console action (TransientCapacityRequest). The broker evaluates current fleet utilization, routing policies, and available surge pools. If approved, the broker issues a lease token with metadata: lease_id, lease_capacity, max_duration, start_ts, billing_mode. Leases can be operator-granted, self-serve via console/SDK, or auto-granted via a policy engine when a tenant hits preconfigured SLOs.

Billing model: default billing is time-pro-rated on allocation duration with two parts: 1) reservation fee: a small flat fee per unit-of-capacity to reserve headroom (charged for the lease duration), and 2) usage fee: actual per-token/per-RPS consumption charged at the tenant's plan rate. If a lease is revoked early (preemption) the reservation fee is pro-rated down to the revocation time and any unused reservation is credited on next invoice. If the broker routes requests into leased headroom but actual request rate is lower than lease_capacity, no penalty beyond the pro-rated reservation fee is applied.

Operator controls and safety: - Admins can set per-tenant daily surge budget and max concurrent leases. - Automatic preemption rules: leases are preemptible if higher-priority tenants request capacity or if underlying host health degrades. Preemption triggers a short grace period (configurable, default 30s) to drain inflight KV cache and gracefully fallback. - Circuit-breakers: if sudden sustained overages occur across fleet, the broker can disable further self-serve leases and surface alerts.

Autoscaling integration: the headroom broker integrates with fleet autoscaling by annotating leases with scale hints (e.g., demand spike signature). Autoscaler will prefer ephemeral burst lanes first, then scale reserved pools only when sustained demand exceeds configured thresholds. This reduces long-term scale churn and keeps unit costs predictable.

Metrics and observability: emit lease.created, lease.approved, lease.revoked, lease.expired, lease.utilization, lease.refund_issued and correlate with per-tenant latency and cost-rate. Add dashboard tile in Console for 'Transient Capacity Activity' with 1h/6h/24h views and estimated invoice impact.

Rollout plan: 1) internal-only pilot on staging fleets (2 weeks) with operator-only grant flow, 2) opt-in beta for select customers with console toggle (4 weeks), 3) general availability with self-serve and billing reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria: - Broker can grant leases and enforce max concurrent leases per tenant. - Billing reconciliation produces expected credits for revoked/unused duration in a test invoice run. - Preemption flow preserves request correctness and latency SLOs within agreed tolerances. - Console shows real-time lease inventory and daily surge spend per tenant.

Risks & mitigations: potential for invoice disputes if timing windows misalign; mitigate by conservative pro-rate windows and clear invoice line-items. Complexity in autoscaler coordination; mitigate by requiring explicit scale hints and running canary autoscaler integration.
